calendar_principles: Treat the 1 March and 1 September plate-change dates as confirmed UK motoring demand moments; treat any internal renewal-peak curve as client-supplied data, not inferred.
Use bank holidays and school holidays as media-consumption context, not as automatic spend increases.
Use BARB and Signal media-market context to decide whether moments are AV, CTV, social, search or OOH opportunities.
Use Signal geo context to distinguish regional household activity from MultiCar and urban growth testing.
Flag unconfirmed or proxy events visibly so agents cannot overclaim source truth.

events.name: New Year reset and bank holiday
events.planning_implication: High availability for family TV, CTV and social consumption. New Year is a natural moment for renewal/switching consideration messaging, not a promotional spike.

events.name: February half-term family window
events.planning_implication: Family routines change and daytime media availability can rise. Useful context for TV, BVOD, YouTube and social creative built around household and MultiCar relevance.

events.name: 1 March plate change with Mother's Day context
events.planning_implication: 1 March is a confirmed UK plate-change date and a genuine registration/new-car demand moment. Mother's Day gifting context can support emotional creative alongside it, but is a context hook, not planning evidence in itself.

events.name: Easter and London Marathon
events.planning_implication: Good Friday and Easter Monday create a long weekend, with higher road-trip and holiday-driving relevance. London Marathon gives a large London attention moment for OOH, local social and PR adjacency if the plan is testing MultiCar or urban growth.

events.name: May bank holidays, half-term and creative platform window
events.planning_implication: May is lower budget in the deterministic plan, but the brief calls for creative-platform development. Use the month for test design, creator/CTV learning and brand platform rehearsal around 'Always Looking Out For You'.

events.name: World Cup opening weeks
events.planning_implication: Football attention fragments media pricing, context and viewing. Use AV and CTV carefully around fixtures, with paid search and social ready for news-driven demand spikes rather than blanket inflation.

events.name: World Cup knockouts, final and school summer break
events.planning_implication: The World Cup final on 19 July and late-July school break create a noisy media month. Keep spend disciplined unless a genuine quote-demand or audience opportunity justifies it.

events.name: Back-to-school build and summer bank holiday
events.planning_implication: Family spending and routine reset rises before September, ahead of the 1 September plate change. This is a useful family-context bridge, but the deterministic plan keeps August lean.

events.name: 1 September plate change, back-to-school reset and London cultural/design season
events.planning_implication: 1 September is the second confirmed UK plate-change date and typically the year's other major registration/new-car demand peak. Back-to-school routine reset can improve planning receptivity; London cultural context supports MultiCar/urban growth testing, but requires a confirmed event feed before client-facing claims.

events.name: October half-term and annual-plan sign-off window
events.planning_implication: A good governance checkpoint before the largest November push. Future versions should freeze signed-off past/future windows separately.

events.name: Largest annual push, Black Friday noise and December build
events.planning_implication: November has the highest deterministic budget in the plan. Black Friday retail noise can inflate attention costs across all advertisers, so rationale must show why Admiral is present and where spend avoids simply chasing inflated CPMs.

events.name: Festive close, Christmas bank holidays and short trading month
events.planning_implication: High emotion and family co-viewing but compressed deadlines and a shorter trading month. Use strong caveats where deadline timing and media delivery collide with Christmas disruption.

agent_calendar_questions: Which events are genuine Admiral planning triggers versus background context?
Which school-holiday source should be treated as the national reference for client sign-off?
Should London event context feed only MultiCar/urban growth planning or all OOH planning?
What event types justify incremental budget rather than just creative or channel phasing changes?
Which calendar claims require a live feed before they can appear in a client export?
